subject: Multi-region node simulation and activation plan for BlueHarbor
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice@blueharbor.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01 09:15 -0800
Subject: Multi-region dedicated capacity ask (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited by the latency and cost controls you showed. We're preparing our Q1 product launch and need Redwood's help sizing dedicated pools for three regions (US east, EU-west, APAC-sg). High level:
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~1.2M inference requests/day by month 3 post-launch.
- Typical request: 1.5k tokens input + 512 tokens generated on our ensemble (two-stage) pipeline.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 750ms for interactive flows; background batch can be higher.
- Models: mix of open Llama3-Chat-medium and a fine-tuned Llama3-Chat-large variant (we can share artifacts).
- Data residency: EU must be isolated; APAC will be mostly Singapore.

Can you provide a proposed node/pool sizing per region, recommended GPU flavor (H100 vs A100/80GB vs L40-class), and an activation timeline (canary -> ramp)? Also need an approximate SOW and procurement lead time for Dedicated.

We have procurement constraints: contract needs to be signed by 2026-12-10 to meet infra timelines.

Appreciate a ballpark by EOD next Monday if possible — we'll use it to brief the heads of engineering.

Cheers,
Alice Park
Head of Platform
BlueHarbor AI

(Attachment: BlueHarbor_initial_requirements.docx)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03 09:42 -0800
Subject: Re: Multi-region dedicated capacity ask (US/EU/APAC)

Connor — ran a short sim (see summary below). I used the following conservative assumptions: 1.2M/day steady-state after month 3; peak/avg ratio 1.6; average total tokens per request (input+output) ~2000; model mix: 60% medium, 40% large; batchable low-latency windows ~20% of traffic (can't batch much); target p95 < 750ms (we budget 600ms on-node).

Summary (recommended starting pools):
- US-east (primary): 16 H100-80GB nodes (estimate sustained throughput ~55 r/s per node for medium; 28 r/s for large with KV cache; continuous batching & prefix cache). Add 6-node burst buffer for peak spikes (can be shared cross-region if routed).
- EU-west (data-isolated): 8 H100-80GB nodes (sustained ~27 r/s per node effective due to EU routing + network overhead). 3-node burst.
- APAC-sg: 6 H100-80GB nodes (higher latency overhead; consider hybrid with A100-80 as cost optimization). 2-node burst.

Alternate cost-optimized (A100-80GB): US 22 nodes, EU 12 nodes, APAC 9 nodes (higher node count due to lower per-node throughput).

Operational notes / constraints:
- Canary: 2-node per-region small canary (H100) for model validation + observability hooks.
- Model pinning: recommend pinning the fine-tuned large to Dedicated in EU and US for SLA critical paths; APAC can start on Hosted fallback for week 1 if procurement delayed.
- Quantization: pipeline supports 4-bit quantization for medium; large requires fp16 to preserve quality — this affects kernel choices and reduces batching efficiency.
- Estimated lead time: 6–8 weeks from SOW signature for node reservation and provisioning (Marcus to confirm contractual ramp clauses and procurement lead times).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm whether BlueHarbor requires model pinning in APAC.
2) Connor to share priority on cost vs latency so we finalize H100 vs A100 split.
3) I will generate a capacity_sim spreadsheet (attached) with per-day token throughput, per-node r/s assumptions, and cost delta rows.

Hannah
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposal: node sizing + activation timeline for BlueHarbor (SOW & next steps)

Alice / Jordan — following our internal simulation and procurement check, please find our proposed starting configuration and timeline below. We attached a lightweight SOW draft and the capacity simulation workbook. This is intended as a starting point for commercial/technical review.

Proposed starting configuration (recommended):
- US-east: 16 x H100-80GB dedicated nodes (sustained), 6-node burst buffer (shared routing).
- EU-west (isolated): 8 x H100-80GB dedicated nodes, 3-node burst.
- APAC-sg: 6 x H100-80GB dedicated nodes with option to substitute 3 A100-80GB for cost smoothing.

Canary & activation plan:
- Week 0 (post-signature): Contract finalized, kick-off, access provisioning.
- Week 2–4: Node reservation and initial canary deployment (2 nodes/region). Canary includes model pinning for EU and US only. SLOs instrumented and E2E tests run.
- Week 5–8: Ramp to sustained nodes; traffic shift using smart routing + fallback to Hosted for APAC if required.

Commercial notes:
- Estimated monthly committed spend (baseline H100 config): $1.05M/month (approximate; final pricing in SOW).
- Procurement lead time: 6 weeks typical for reserved capacity; surge clauses available for faster activation with premium. Marcus will work with procurement to add explicit lead-time SLAs in the SOW.

Deliverables attached: BlueHarbor_SOW_v0.3.pdf (draft SOW with milestones, acceptance criteria, and SLA language) and Capacity_Sim_Q1Q2.xlsx (detailed per-node throughput and cost rows).

Requested actions:
1) Alice/Jordan: confirm whether APAC model pinning is required or tolerated to start on Hosted fallback (reply by 2026-11-24 to meet procurement timeline).
2) BlueHarbor procurement: review the SOW draft and provide any contract redlines by 2026-11-30.
3) Connor/Redwood: prepare commercial term sheet once APAC decision is made.

Thanks — happy to hop on a joint call to walk through the simulation.

Best regards,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
